status: declared by the pull request that closes #383 (track E of #374) before any score was computed; the choices it leaves to Eleonora (the threshold u, the scale's covariates, the shape bound, the minimum number of excesses) are listed in that pull request

model.structure: P(spread > tau) = P(spread > u) * S(tau - u)
model.body: scikit-learn LogisticRegression, C = 1.0, L2, columns standardised on the fit rows (ml.PRESSURE_LOGISTIC_SETTINGS), fitted to the label spread > u on the direct pressure design (spread, the three calendar types alone and times reserves, reserves, the TGA change alone and times reserves)
model.tail: generalised Pareto survival S of the excess over u + 0.5 bp, the spread being published to the basis point: an observation is the bin [k - u - 1, k - u) of the excess, its likelihood S(k - u - 1) - S(k - u), and a forecast of spread > tau is S(tau - u)
model.scale: sigma = exp(b0 + b . x) on the standardised columns reserves (USD trillions), quarter end, month end, tax date, ridge-penalised with C = 1.0, the intercept free
model.shape: one constant per fit, 0.5 * expit(s): inside ml.GPD_SHAPE_BOUNDS (0, 0.5), the floor of docs/decisions/tail-shape-floor.md
model.estimator: maximum likelihood by BFGS with a finite-difference gradient, numpy only (ml.fit_censored_gpd)
model.minimum_excesses: 30: a fit with fewer excesses is an exponential (shape 0) with one constant scale; none at all gives tail probability 0
model.labels: the body is fitted to the label spread > u and the tail to the excesses above it, the rare event the +5 bp and +10 bp labels are nested in, never an all-days loss; the +5 bp and +10 bp labels are what the diagnostics and the judge score
model.treasury_settlement: left out: its size is public one business day ahead only (#170)
